title: Exploring Electronics
description: Electronics from first principles — voltage, current, resistance, and circuit design explained clearly. Real components, real numbers, no prior knowledge assumed.

items.title: Home
items.content_html: Electronics from first principles — voltage, current, resistance, and circuit design explained clearly. Real components, real numbers, no prior knowledge assumed.

items.title: Reading an Analog Sensor
items.content_html: Digital pins only know HIGH and LOW. Wire an MCP9700A temperature sensor to an Arduino and use analogRead() to measure a continuous voltage instead.

items.title: Blink an LED
items.content_html: Wire a single-LED circuit on a breadboard and flash the Blink sketch to an Arduino — your first complete loop from wiring to running code on real hardware.

items.title: Digital Pins
items.content_html: A digital pin is either on or off — nothing in between. Learn how a microcontroller drives an LED and reads a button, and why each pin needs a resistor.

items.title: Package Types
items.content_html: Every component has a physical shape called a package. Learn the common through-hole and surface-mount families, and why this site's parts are all one kind.

items.title: Pull-up and Pull-down Resistors
items.content_html: An unconnected input pin floats and reads noise. How pull-up and pull-down resistors give it a steady HIGH or LOW, which to choose, and how to size one.

items.title: How to Read a Schematic
items.content_html: Learn to read electronics schematics: the standard symbols for resistors, capacitors, LEDs, and transistors, and how to trace current through any circuit.

items.title: Resistor Color Codes
items.content_html: A resistor has no printed numbers — just colored stripes. Learn what each band means and how to decode any resistor's value and tolerance on sight.

items.title: Series and Parallel Circuits
items.content_html: Two wiring patterns govern every circuit ever built. Learn how series and parallel circuits work — why voltage divides in one and stays constant in the other.

items.title: Temperature Sensors
items.content_html: A microcontroller can only measure voltage. Learn how thermistors, analog ICs, and digital sensors each turn heat into something a circuit can read.

items.title: Building a Threshold Ladder
items.content_html: Turn one sensor reading into staged, at-a-glance output. Wire three LEDs to an Arduino and light one, two, or three based on distance from baseline.

items.title: What Is an Arduino?
items.content_html: An Arduino is a tiny dedicated computer on a board. Learn what's actually on it, and how to read your first lines of Arduino code line by line.

items.title: What Is Electricity?
items.content_html: The label on your USB charger says 5V ⎓ 2A. Two numbers that explain how electricity works — voltage, current, resistance, and Ohm's Law explained clearly.

items.title: arduino-cli
items.content_html: Compile and upload Arduino sketches from the terminal with arduino-cli — one command, no IDE. Install it, find your board, and flash code from your own editor.

items.title: Breadboards
items.content_html: How breadboard holes connect internally, how to use the power rails, and the wiring mistakes that kill every beginner's first circuit before it even starts.
